office_policy: Map P39 QIDs only, never office labels or similar strings. Only exact_office rows can propose an office equivalence; family_only and external_only require separate historical research. No claim of actual power or continuity of legal jurisdiction.

mappings.note: Emperor of all the Russias is a legal imperial title. Does not assert practical dominance.
Chairman of the Supreme Soviet of USSR; do not conflate with Presidium chair.

Chairman of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Soviet, a juridical collective-body chair (1938–May 1989). Different office from Chairman of the Supreme Soviet (Q4376657, canonical vs-ussr); neither title proves actual personal dominance or certifies an individual's tenure dates.
Chairman of USSR Council of Ministers from 1946; not Council of People's Commissars or composite legacy-g06.
Wikidata item groups general secretary and first secretary; canon distinguishes titles, Stalin 1934 changes, and leadership interpretations.
King of Prussia is a foreign juridical office and has no v1 canonical office ID.
Elective Holy Roman emperor office; not sovereign nationality, territory, or Habsburg composite monarchy.
USSR Council of People's Commissars chairman 1923–1946. Not the RSFSR SNK, nor the Council of Ministers after 1946; composite legacy-g06 remains unmapped and source-reviewed.

Generic transhistorical regent title is only a family-level comparison with existing Russian regent roles. Sophia (1682–1689), Elena Glinskaya (1533–1538) and Anna Leopoldovna (1740–1741) governed under different legal and institutional circumstances; not independent sovereign monarchs. Do not infer actual authority or accept P39 day precision from the office QID.

The broad Prince/Grand Duke of Moscow item is an office FAMILY, not automatically the same as distinct grand prince of all Rus or Tsar of Russia. Cross-reference Vasily I and Dmitry Shemyaka, but P39 Shemyaka 1445 conflicts with historical scholarship placing formal reign February 1446–February 1447. P39 also associates Aleksei Mikhailovich (1645–1676), a Tsardom sovereign: preserve an explicit unmatched context warning instead of fabricating a Moscow grand-princely tenure.

Historically scoped Tsar of All Russia office type; not the pre-1547 Moscow grand prince, post-1721 Emperor of Russia, or proof of sovereign power over all claimed territory. Boris Godunov was elected in 1598; Peter I inherited the Tsar title 1682 and was granted the Emperor title on 22 October Julian/2 November Gregorian 1721. Time qualifier and continuity require independent review.
